title: k-fold CRT, Pi-type form: ℤ/(∏ nᵢ)ℤ ≅ ∏_{i:Fin k} ℤ/nᵢℤ
description: The k-fold Chinese Remainder Theorem in its canonical dependent-product (Pi-type) form, indexed symmetrically by Fin k. For a pairwise-coprime family ns : Fin k → ℕ, the ring ZMod (∏ i, ns i) is isomorphic to the dependent product ∀ i : Fin k, ZMod (ns i). This answers the third open question of the parent k-fold CRT entry, which proved the list/nested-pair form ZMod ns.prod ≃+* CRTProd ns with a right-associated PUnit tower. The Pi-type form is the standard textbook statement and is reusable as an indexed product (no nested pairs). Constructed directly by induction on k: the base case uses that ZMod 1 and the empty Pi-type are both subsingletons; the step splits off the head ns 0 via Fin.prod_univ_succ, applies the binary ZMod.chineseRemainder with head-coprime-to-tail-product, recurses, and reassembles with a Fin.cons ring isomorphism. Includes bijectivity, ring-hom properties, a round-trip identity, the cardinality consequence |∏ᵢ ZMod nᵢ| = ∏ nᵢ, and a concrete ℤ/30ℤ ≅ ∏ ℤ/[2,3,5]ᵢℤ example.

overview.historicalContext: The Chinese Remainder Theorem originates in Sunzi Suanjing (~3rd century CE) and was given a general algorithm by Qin Jiushao (1247) and systematic treatment by Gauss in Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801). Modern algebra recasts it as a ring isomorphism. Two formulations coexist: the right-associated list/nested-pair form (convenient for induction over a List) and the symmetric dependent-product (Pi-type) form ∏_{i:Fin k} ℤ/nᵢℤ indexed by Fin k. The Pi-type form is the canonical textbook statement and the one that composes cleanly with other indexed constructions (e.g. ring structure on dependent function types, unit-group decompositions). This entry bridges the parent's list form to the Pi-type form.
overview.problemStatement:
**Theorem (crtPi)**: For a pairwise-coprime family ns : Fin k → ℕ (i ≠ j ⟹ Coprime (ns i) (ns j)),
  ZMod (∏ i, ns i) ≃+* ∀ i : Fin k, ZMod (ns i)
as rings, indexed symmetrically by Fin k.
overview.text: A 217-line formalization of the k-fold Chinese Remainder Theorem in its dependent-product (Pi-type) form ℤ/(∏ nᵢ)ℤ ≅ ∏_{i:Fin k} ℤ/nᵢℤ, answering the third open question of the parent list-form entry. Two structural ring isomorphisms do the work: `ringEquivOfSubsingleton` (any two subsingleton commutative rings are isomorphic) for the k = 0 base, and `finSplitRingEquiv` (a dependent product over Fin (k+1) splits as head factor times the tail product, with the ring-hom laws holding on the nose by rfl). The main isomorphism `crtPi` is built by induction on k: each step splits ∏ via `Fin.prod_univ_succ`, applies binary `ZMod.chineseRemainder` using `head_coprime_tail_prod`, recurses on the tail family, and reassembles the Pi-type with `finSplitRingEquiv.symm`. Properties (bijectivity, ring-hom, round-trip) follow from the RingEquiv API; `crtPi_card` derives |∏ᵢ ZMod nᵢ| = ∏ nᵢ. Fully verified: 0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Induction on k (the number of moduli)**:

**Base (k = 0)**: The empty product ∏ i : Fin 0, ns i = 1, so the source is ZMod 1, a subsingleton; the target ∀ i : Fin 0, _ is also a subsingleton. `ringEquivOfSubsingleton` supplies the (unique) isomorphism.

**Step (k+1)**:
1. `Fin.prod_univ_succ` rewrites ∏ i, ns i = ns 0 · ∏ i : Fin k, ns i.succ.
2. `head_coprime_tail_prod` gives Coprime (ns 0) (∏ tail), so binary `ZMod.chineseRemainder` yields ZMod (∏) ≃+* ZMod (ns 0) × ZMod (∏ tail).
3. The inductive hypothesis on the tail family (via `pairwise_tail`) gives ZMod (∏ tail) ≃+* ∀ i : Fin k, ZMod (ns i.succ); lift it into the second factor with `RingEquiv.prodCongr`.
4. Reassemble the Pi-type via `finSplitRingEquiv.symm`.
Compose the three RingEquivs.
keyInsights: Indexing by Fin k (not a List) gives the symmetric, reusable product form — the standard CRT statement — at the cost of a Fin.cons reassembly step

finSplitRingEquiv is a ring isomorphism whose map_mul'/map_add' are literally rfl: products and sums on dependent function types are pointwise, so splitting off the head commutes with the ring operations definitionally
The k = 0 base avoids ZMod (∏ Fin 0) ≠ ZMod 1 friction by rewriting the empty product to 1 and invoking a generic subsingleton ring isomorphism
head_coprime_tail_prod packages Nat.Coprime.prod_right: the head is coprime to every tail factor (each indexed by i.succ ≠ 0), hence to their product
Cardinality preservation is a free corollary: a ring bijection transports Nat.card, and Nat.card (ZMod N) = N for N ≠ 0, giving ∏ᵢ |ZMod nᵢ| = ∏ nᵢ
Example coprimality is discharged by kernel `decide`, keeping the entry axiom-free (no native_decide / Lean.ofReduceBool)

sections.title: Two Structural Ring Isomorphisms
sections.summary: ringEquivOfSubsingleton: any two subsingleton commutative rings are ring-isomorphic (k = 0 base case). finSplitRingEquiv: a dependent product over Fin (k+1) splits as head factor times the tail product, with map_mul'/map_add' true by rfl and inverse given by Fin.cons.
sections.mathContext: Two reusable ring isomorphisms. (1) If A, B are subsingleton commutative rings, the constant-zero map A → B is a ring isomorphism (everything collapses to 0). (2) The map f ↦ (f 0, fun i ↦ f i.succ) is a ring isomorphism (∀ i : Fin (k+1), M i) ≃+* M 0 × (∀ i : Fin k, M i.succ); pointwise operations make the homomorphism laws hold definitionally, and Fin.cons is the inverse.

sections.title: Coprimality of Head with Tail Product
sections.summary: head_coprime_tail_prod: for a pairwise-coprime family, ns 0 is coprime to ∏ i : Fin k, ns i.succ (via Nat.Coprime.prod_right, since i.succ ≠ 0). pairwise_tail: the tail family ns ∘ succ is itself pairwise coprime.
sections.mathContext: To apply the binary CRT at each step we need gcd(ns 0, ∏_{i} ns(i+1)) = 1. This follows from Nat.Coprime.prod_right because ns 0 is coprime to each ns(i+1) (their indices 0 and i.succ differ). The tail's pairwise coprimality is inherited from the whole family via injectivity of Fin.succ, feeding the inductive hypothesis.

sections.title: The k-fold CRT (Pi-type form)
sections.summary: crtPi: the main construction. Induction on k. Base: rewrite ∏ Fin 0 = 1 and use ringEquivOfSubsingleton. Step: Fin.prod_univ_succ splits the product, ZMod.chineseRemainder gives the binary split, the IH handles the tail, RingEquiv.prodCongr lifts it, and finSplitRingEquiv.symm reassembles the Pi-type.
sections.mathContext: The isomorphism ZMod (∏ i, ns i) ≃+* ∀ i : Fin k, ZMod (ns i) is built by induction. At step k+1: ZMod (∏) ≃ ZMod (ns 0) × ZMod (∏ tail) [binary CRT] ≃ ZMod (ns 0) × (∀ i : Fin k, ZMod (ns i.succ)) [IH lifted by prodCongr] ≃ ∀ i : Fin (k+1), ZMod (ns i) [Fin.cons reassembly]. The cast hprod ▸ aligns ZMod (∏) with ZMod (ns 0 * ∏ tail).

sections.title: Properties
sections.summary: crtPi_bijective, crtPi_map_mul, crtPi_map_add, crtPi_symm_apply_apply from the RingEquiv API. crtPi_card: cardinality preservation Nat.card (∀ i, ZMod (ns i)) = ∏ i, ns i for positive moduli, by transporting Nat.card across the bijection and using ZMod.card.
sections.mathContext: Since crtPi is a RingEquiv, it is automatically bijective and preserves +, ×, and round-trips. The cardinality consequence: a ring bijection preserves Nat.card, and for positive moduli Nat.card (ZMod (∏ nᵢ)) = ∏ nᵢ, so |∏ᵢ ZMod nᵢ| = ∏ nᵢ. This recovers the multiplicative count |ℤ/Nℤ| = ∏ |ℤ/nᵢℤ|.

crossReferences.description: Direct parent: the k-fold CRT in list/nested-pair form ZMod ns.prod ≃+* CRTProd ns. This entry answers its third open question by giving the symmetric Pi-type form indexed by Fin k.
Grandparent: the 2-fold CRT and its ring-theoretic formulation, the base case applied at every inductive step here.
The Pi-type CRT preserves units, so the unit group ∏ᵢ (ℤ/nᵢℤ)* factors symmetrically — the structural source of k-fold totient multiplicativity.
Unique prime factorization n = ∏ pᵢ^{aᵢ} supplies a canonical pairwise-coprime family Fin k → ℕ, making the Pi-type CRT directly applicable to any modulus.

conclusion.summary: Answers the parent's third open question: the k-fold CRT holds in the canonical dependent-product (Pi-type) form ZMod (∏ i, ns i) ≃+* ∀ i : Fin k, ZMod (ns i), indexed symmetrically by Fin k. Built by induction on k from binary ZMod.chineseRemainder and a Fin.cons ring isomorphism, with 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide. Cardinality preservation and a concrete ℤ/30ℤ example are included.
conclusion.implications: **For algebra**: the Pi-type form is the reusable indexed product — it composes with dependent-function ring structure and unit-group decompositions, unlike the right-associated list form. **For Mathlib**: a candidate symmetric companion to ZMod.chineseRemainder over Fin k.
